Workshop

workshop (app id dev.mixos.workshop) is a native window onto the Bus of the node it runs on. It asks noded which services are registered, asks each service to describe its commands, and shows them as a tree. Select a command to read its arguments and description, type a JSON body, and call it. The reply is shown with its return code. Workshop also lists the mesh nodes this node can see.

It is for people and agents who want to see what a node offers and try a command by hand. It ships in the mixos-desktop package set. Nothing else in the workspace depends on it.

Workshop is also the reference app for driving a window over the Bus. Everything in its window is a Bus command, and Driving apps over the Bus uses it as the worked example.

The source is apps/workshop.

How it is built

Saved arrangement

Workshop uses toolkit's shared saved-window store at <AppDirs::state()>/window.conf.mix. With the ordinary XDG defaults this is $XDG_STATE_HOME/mixos/apps/workshop/state/window.conf.mix, or ~/.local/state/mixos/apps/workshop/state/window.conf.mix without that variable. AppDirs overrides are honoured.

It saves the selected command and row key, expanded tree rows, services search, macro-window visibility, Traffic side, open and paused state and filter, the services and Traffic panel shares, services scroll and the Details outer scroll keyed by selection. The five window theme choices remain independent; following the session stays following it. Inner size and maximised state are restored on every desktop. On compd, output, position and workspace are also remembered, without changing the user's current workspace. Plasma and other Wayland desktops do not save or restore position, output or workspace.

Selection and expansion return as live rows appear; restoring a selection does not call or run anything. Keys absent after discovery are dropped. Keeping the selected row visible takes priority over an old scroll offset. Request bodies, dialogs, keyboard focus, replies and Traffic rows are not saved. Reply and Traffic views start empty. Headless runs and tests use memory only unless a test explicitly injects its own directory.

Writes are atomic, changed-only and coalesced, with a final flush at exit. Malformed files or future store schemas load defaults and are preserved untouched. workshop.info includes the toolkit's saved-state description.

Workshop follows the engine-first rule in AGENTS.md §4.1. It is two crates:

  • inspector (crates/inspector): the headless engine. No UI and no I/O. It holds the protocol model, the discovery and call rules, and the handling of every workshop.* command.
  • workshop: the egui shell. It draws the engine's state, runs the engine's effects on a small tokio runtime, and owns the command registry that the menus, the shortcuts and the Bus all go through.

The engine never does work itself. The shell feeds it events (Bus deliveries, finished discoveries and calls, edits made in the window), and the engine returns Effects for the shell to carry out: Discover, Call, Show, Reply, Commands, Execute, Describe, Drive, Copy and Exit. Every effect that leaves the process carries a ticket. A completion whose ticket is not the one in flight is ignored, so a late reply can never land on a newer operation.

inspector

ModuleWhat it holds
modelCommand, Snapshot (services, each with its commands or an error; peers), Selection, the parsers for noded.list, noded.peers, HELP and app.describe, the limits, and describe(), the app's own command list
engineEngine, Effect, Dialog, Row and RowKind (the services tree), UiState (what a person arranges), Session (the session theme)
meshbounded per-link and local traffic tally, event windows, reply correlation, topology, pings and injectable clock
busthe connection, through the shared citizen library: start, probe, forward, show, and discover

Discovery reads noded.info, noded.list and noded.peers. The local node appears first, followed by sorted peers. Each peer is queried through noded.<node>.bus, then its services through <service>.<node>.bus. Local membership and service identities are published as soon as they arrive, without waiting for remote nodes or command descriptions. Discovery queries up to eight remote nodes concurrently, with a separate local slot. Each read has a three-second deadline (DISCOVERY_CALL_BUDGET); info and list run together. Across all nodes and refreshes, at most twelve discovery calls run at once: six reserved for local reads and six shared by remote reads. A cancelled description retains its permit until the native request finishes. Discovery asks for HELP, falling back to app.describe, eight services at a time per node, with a three-second budget for the description phase. Every node update wakes the view. The status counts completed nodes and unreachable nodes; unreachable rows include the reason and refresh retries them. Failed discovery and descriptions appear beneath the affected node or service. Each service retains its ServiceInfo; labels show version and short SHA when advertised, and Details shows the full identity including binary and dirty state.

The limits are fixed in model:

  • a JSON body is at most 65,536 bytes;
  • a reply is shown up to 1,000,000 bytes, then marked as truncated.

workshop

ModuleWhat it holds
src/main.rsoptions, single-instance launch, the eframe window
src/lib.rsthe string catalogue: strings(), label(), label_with()
src/shell.rsShell: applies events, settles effects, runs Bus work, follows the desktop profile, wires the toolkit drive layer
src/view.rsview(): draws the engine's state and returns what the person did as UiEvents; it never changes state itself
src/mesh.rsthe native Mesh map, accessible nodes and links, and bounded dot animation state
src/commands.rsregistry(): every command, with its menu, shortcut, icon and when it is enabled
i18n/en/workshop.ftlthe English strings

The shell applies one event and settles its effects before it reads the next, so a later delivery can never change what an earlier command acts on. Within one frame, edits are applied before commands, so a call uses the body the person sees. Bus work wakes the window only when something finished; nothing polls.

Rules

  • One operation at a time. A refresh or a call in flight makes the window busy. Bus requests that need it idle are refused with BUSY.
  • A call is sent once. Workshop never retries. A transport failure is reported as return code 10 with the outcome unknown.
  • No call on bad input. An unadvertised target, a body over the limit or invalid JSON is refused before anything is sent. An empty body is allowed.
  • Closing answers everything. Quit waits until accepted work is finished, and every Bus request already accepted gets an answer before the connection stops.
  • One window per session. A second launch finds the running Workshop on the Bus, asks it to show its window through compd, and exits.

Bus

Workshop registers as workshop on the local broker. Its commands are registered in commands.conf.mix with owner workshop.

  • Reading: workshop.ping, workshop.info, workshop.tree, workshop.reply, workshop.actions, workshop.mesh, plus HELP and app.describe.
  • Changing state: workshop.filter, workshop.expand, workshop.select_row, workshop.select, workshop.body, workshop.split, workshop.dock, workshop.dialog, workshop.theme, workshop.call, workshop.execute, workshop.refresh, workshop.show, workshop.quit, workshop.mesh.ping.
  • The window's drive commands, from the toolkit: workshop.ui.tree, workshop.ui.click, workshop.ui.pointer, workshop.ui.scroll, workshop.ui.key, workshop.ui.type, workshop.ui.menu, workshop.ui.menu.list, workshop.ui.menu.open, workshop.ui.menu.close, workshop.ui.capture, workshop.window and workshop.window.state.

Arguments, answers and refusal codes (BUSY, DISCONNECTED, ARGUMENT, UNKNOWN_COMMAND, UNKNOWN_ACTION, DISABLED) are tabled in Driving apps over the Bus. Tree rows use node:<node>, service:<node>:<service> and command:<node>:<service>:<command>, for example node:alpha, service:alpha:noded and command:alpha:noded:noded.list. A command selection keeps its routed service address so calls reach the selected node.

Calling a command from Mix through Workshop:

$body = json_encode({service: "noded", command: "noded.list"})
send workshop workshop.call body=$body timeout=30
print $result

The answer is {service, command, request_body, rc, body}.

View › Theme adds the view.theme.*, view.mode.*, view.style.*, view.decorations.* and view.captions.* choices. They set the theme of this window only; the session's theme file is never written. The Help menu opens with a field that searches every command. The desktop profile can rebind the shortcuts (keymaps.workshop.<id>), and workshop.actions reports the ones in force.

Mesh map

Select Nodes → Mesh (nodes:mesh) to draw this node in the centre and its peers around an ellipse in Details. Selecting Mesh refreshes noded.info and noded.peers, and starts the same observation stream as Traffic's Observe traffic action if it is off. Reconnecting refreshes the nodes and restarts observation only if it was enabled before disconnecting. Turning Observe off shows Observation stopped and a Start observation button; selecting Mesh again also starts it. A refused stream shows the broker's reason in Details. Observation subscribed reports the subscription state; the last-event age reports receipt time without claiming that a quiet stream is live. Traffic naming a peer absent from the map triggers a topology refresh, with at most one refresh in flight.

Each spoke has separate outgoing and incoming curves. Their widths follow the last five minutes of messages. Dots show observed messages in their original order and spacing; replies launch after the request's travel time. Rejected and dropped messages use the theme's danger colour. Local messages make an expanding ring. Animation requests repaints only while moving, with one scheduled wake for a delayed dot. A visible Mesh view also repaints once per second to update ages and window widths. It schedules no age repaint when hidden or when another row is selected, and this wake never polls the Bus. Typed tally summaries are cached by tally revision and wall-clock second; geometry is reused until the map rectangle, peers, font unit or theme changes.

Hover or focus a node to read its counts since start, over one minute and five minutes, top services and commands, and its latest ping and age. The local node panel includes local service traffic and totals across mesh links. Every map node is keyboard focusable and has a distinct accessible name, for example beta · mesh peer or alpha · this node. Use workshop.ui.click {label:"beta · mesh peer"} to click the map; tree nodes keep their plain names, such as beta. Clicking a map node selects its node:<name> tree row; clicking a spoke opens Traffic filtered to its peer.

Ping peers in Details or Bus → Ping peers (mesh.ping) pings each known peer once, sequentially, with a two-second deadline per peer. Nothing pings on a timer. A failed ping leaves a danger ring until inbound traffic from that peer or a newer successful ping clears it. Ping age is measured from each peer's completion, rather than the start of the whole round.

workshop.mesh {} reads the map as JSON: this_node, peers, nodes, links (message and byte totals, out_1m, in_1m, out_5m, in_5m, top services and commands), local, probe.results (including age_ms), observer (observation state, error and dropped counters), nodes_error, and recent. workshop.mesh.ping {} starts a round and immediately returns {pinging:["beta","gamma"]}; read workshop.mesh for its results. Both commands accept every caller, local or mesh. Overlapping ping rounds return BUSY; no known peers returns UNAVAILABLE.

Only this node's broker is observed. Dashed links between peers represent traffic that Workshop cannot see. Broker events with peer identify the link directly. Older events fall back to mesh addresses and reply correlation IDs; unidentifiable messages appear in the unnamed-node count. Workshop excludes its own observe, discovery and ping traffic from the tally. Named peers outside the bounded map appear in unplaced-peer rows with their message counts; overflow beyond the bounded link tally joins the unnamed count. Future broker timestamps are clamped to receipt time for buckets; a clock step back discards buckets more than five seconds ahead. Pausing Traffic does not pause the map, and its counters are independent of Traffic's ring.

workshop.tree identifies the map with key nodes:mesh and kind mesh_map. The peers group retains key mesh and kind peers. Saved arrangements from before the Nodes root open that root once; later deliberate collapses survive.

All retained state is bounded: 64 named traffic links plus an unknown link, 40 distinct count keys plus an overflow key, 2,000 pending correlations, 2,000 recent events over 15 seconds, and a five-minute second-bucket window (301 slots including the lower boundary, matching the reference tally). The node list and ping results are capped at 64 peers. Retained event labels are limited to 256 characters; oversized correlation IDs are not matched.

Traffic dock

Traffic uses the right pane when Auto sees a window at least 1280 logical pixels wide, and the bottom pane otherwise. View › Traffic placement selects Auto, Bottom or Right; the dock header's panel button switches between Bottom and Right. Drag the pane boundary to resize it. Placement, right width and bottom height are saved in the window's UiState, with separate sizes for each side. Width is kept within 20–50% of the window, height within 12–50%. The services split is a share of the width left beside Traffic, within 10–80%. workshop.dock {side:"auto", size} records the requested share on both axes (each within its own limits), so the size survives the first layout and later crossings of Auto's width threshold. Startup resolves Auto from the saved window width before the first frame.

Click Traffic in its header (or View › Traffic) to collapse it to a bottom header strip; click again to reopen it. Right-side rows show time, command, return code and milliseconds on the first line, with sender, service and direction beneath. Both layouts expand a row to show its retained JSON.

workshop.dock {side:"auto"|"bottom"|"right", size?:number, open?:bool} sets placement, optionally the active side's share (0–1, clamped to the limits above) and whether the dock is open. Invalid values return ARGUMENT without changing state. In Auto, size applies to the side used by the current window (Bottom in a headless instance). workshop.info reports ui.dock_side, ui.dock_effective, ui.dock_size, ui.dock_width and ui.dock_height.

Running it

workshop [--headless] [--noded-url URL] [--service NAME] [--comp NAME]
  • --noded-url: the broker to use. The default is the session's noded.
  • --headless: run the same engine and Bus port without a native window or renderer. Repaint events wake the logic thread. Use a distinct --service name for a test instance; duplicate registrations are refused.
  • --service: the Bus name to register as, workshop by default.
  • --comp: the compositor's service name, used to raise the window. The default is $MIXOS_COMP_SERVICE, or comp.

Service names may contain only ASCII letters, digits, -, _ and ..

The window follows the desktop profile's look and keymaps from settingsd, through the settings follower, and updates when they change. With no theme chosen it starts in Studio Dark.

Testing

On an authorised build worker at a pushed commit:

cargo test --locked -p inspector -p workshop
  • The engine's unit tests (crates/inspector/src/engine.rs, model.rs) cover discovery, selection, the body, calls, the Bus commands, refusals, tickets and quitting, with no UI.
  • tests/shell.rs runs the real Shell on a logging Bus handle (the inspector testing feature) and checks every reply, call and the final quit in order.
  • tests/drive.rs drives the window over its Bus commands against the real view: clicks, typing, the title bar controls, menus.
  • tests/view.rs checks the dialogs, the body buttons and their tooltips, and the search field through kittest.
  • tests/snapshot.rs takes offscreen snapshots in several themes into tests/snapshots/. Regenerate with UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1 and look at the images before committing them.
  • crates/inspector/src/mesh.rs ports the Mesh Watch tally oracle with public example names and addresses, plus bounds, expiry, pause and engine effect tests. tests/mesh.rs checks accessible map controls and node panels; tests/drive.rs also drives map nodes and links through workshop.ui.click. The map snapshots mesh_studio_dark.png and mesh_pro_light.png use a fixed clock and no animation.
  • tests/registry.rs checks that the command registry lists exactly the commands Workshop describes, and that read-only commands are class query (command classes).
  • crates/inspector/tests/native.rs runs discovery, calls and single-instance registration against an isolated real broker. It is ignored by default and needs WORKSHOP_TEST_URL.
  • crates/inspector/tests/discovery.rs uses a fake broker with a node that never replies. Local and healthy rows arrive before its timeout, discovery settles within a bounded time, and the next refresh retries the failed node.

Macro Bus commands

The shared macro Bus surface uses this process's catalogue and runner. Subscribe to <service>.macros.finished for completion, where service is the instance’s registered Bus name (for example term-1234 for a second Term instance). Commands keep the app’s canonical prefix, such as workshop.macros.run.

CommandArgumentsResult
workshop.macros.list{}Catalogue and diagnostics
workshop.macros.reload{}Catalogue and diagnostics
workshop.macros.run{id}Acceptance and run number
workshop.macros.status{}Current or last run
workshop.macros.output{}Retained output and dropped flag
workshop.macros.stop{}Whether termination was requested
workshop.macros.new{app,title}Create a user macro, select it and open its document; returns {app,id,path,text,tier,catalogue}
workshop.macros.get{id, app?}Read {id,tier,path,text}, at most 256 KiB
workshop.macros.put{id,text,app?}Save a user macro atomically and refresh its owning Session
workshop.macros.remove{id,app?}Delete a user macro; built-ins refuse with DENIED
workshop.macros.move{id,tier,app?,destination?}Move between user tiers; refuse a destination clash
workshop.macros.copy{id,app?}Copy a built-in into its corresponding user tier
workshop.macros.open{app,id?}Select a macro in Details, or expand the app's branch
workshop.traffic{limit?,filter?}Read up to 1,024 retained rows and the dropped count
workshop.observe{on,filter?,body?}Start or stop observation; body defaults to redacted

The global branch has the stable key macros:global. Global user files live directly in the user macro root, for example /home/user/.config/mixos/macros/mesh-ping.mix. Workshop owns their Session. App branches prefer the running app's catalogue and use the Library only when the app is stopped, with a “not running” label. Running an app macro while its app is stopped refuses with UNAVAILABLE. app selects the source app; omit it or use global for globals. Moving a global into an app requires tier: "user-app" and destination: "ced", for example.

Details uses the shared editor document. Save (Ctrl+S), Run (Ctrl+Enter), Stop, Copy to user, Move, Delete with confirmation, Open in Ced and Show in Dopus dispatch through Workshop's command registry. A -- target: header offers only its allowed apps; any offers running apps. The chosen app is passed as MIXOS_MACRO_TARGET. Without a header, Run remains target-free. Each app serves the same management commands through its own macro Session. Select a macro group (macros:<app> or macros:global) or an existing macro and choose Macros → New macro…, or use the New macro… button in Details. Enter a title and choose Create. Workshop refreshes the catalogue, selects the new file and gives its editor the keyboard. The action is available while Workshop is idle. workshop.execute {id:"macro.new"} opens the same dialog; workshop.macros.new {app:"ced",title:"Tidy imports"} creates and opens it directly. Running apps receive their own macros.new request; stopped apps and global macros use the shared local library. Macro requests are capped at 8 KiB, except put: its envelope is capped at 1544 KiB and its text at 256 KiB.

The collapsible Traffic dock combines broker observations and native <service>.action.executed / <service>.macros.finished topics. It retains at most 1,024 rows and 8 MiB, reports dropped rows and redacts sensitive topic fields before retaining them. Broker observation defaults to redacted bodies; none is also supported. A refused observer leaves the reason in the dock and keeps topic deliveries available. Any caller may observe. Run mix --serve tools/workshop_observe.mix --name workshop-probe to check the advertised observe extension and open and close a probe stream.

Open Workshop in an app's macro menu launches or focuses Workshop; a launch with --app ced --id tidy-imports selects that macro. The global folder in Dopus is the fallback when Workshop is not installed. Headless instances use the same management and traffic commands.

Every macro command accepts every caller, local or mesh. This includes global writes, moves between apps, workshop.execute for macro.* and bus.call, and workshop.call with an explicit or selected target. Built-in files remain read-only; path containment, argument validation, request limits and the runner’s single-flight limit still apply.
